summary: Manifest is a backend platform configured entirely through a single YAML file, aiming to simplify server-side development. It falls into the low-code category, allowing developers to set up database structures and logic without writing extensive traditional code. The project is open-source under the MIT licence and built on Node.js.
goodFor: It suits developers who want to rapidly prototype applications or build internal tools without manually scaffolding a complex backend stack.
watchOut: Relying on a single configuration file for an entire backend can introduce scaling or customisation limits when your application outgrows standard low-code patterns.
deployNotes: As a Node.js application, you will typically need to run it behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS and configure persistent storage for any underlying data it generates.
